$description: Semantic colours in the light scheme.

primary.$description: Text that reads first: body copy, names, values.

secondary.$description: Text that reads second: meta, hints, labels, a place that is not current.

tertiary.$description: Text that reads third: counts, context lines, section labels, the key bar.

negative.$description: Errors and destructive outcomes; a Blocked chip's words.

warning.$description: The Warn tone: a Warn chip's words, and the glyph of a Warn notice or outcome.

positive.$description: The Go tone: a Go chip's words.

onStatusFill.$description: Text on the warning fill: a Mark, a stale link's state.

red.$description: Terminal output and syntax only, never chrome. Each reads at AA on background.head.

green.$description: Terminal output and syntax only, never chrome.

yellow.$description: Terminal output and syntax only, never chrome.

blue.$description: Terminal output and syntax only, never chrome.

magenta.$description: Terminal output and syntax only, never chrome.

cyan.$description: Terminal output and syntax only, never chrome.

primary.$description: The edge of a control at 3:1 on any ground: a field, an unchecked box; and the lines that contain panels and cards.

secondary.$description: The ring of a button or key hint, and the containing line of a held or quiet control.

divider.$description: Lines that divide: rows, sections, a sidebar's edge; also a meter's empty track. Decorative, never the only cue for a control.

negative.$description: The line of an invalid or destructive control.

secondary.$description: Keyboard focus on a row, and the border of a reel's focused pane: quieter than the default ring.

negative.$description: Keyboard focus on an invalid control.

sidebar.$description: The full-height sidebar at the page's left.

surface.$description: Panels, cards, dialogs and controls; the current place in a sidebar.

head.$description: The sunken ground: a table head, a shelf, code and its marks, a count's box, and what is lifted or a drop lands on. Never a hover tint; that is background.hover.

hover.$description: The tint under a hovered row, place or quiet button.

selected.$description: The tint under what is selected or current: a row, a menu choice, the current page or place, a pressed segment. Its text keeps its colour: every text tone and border.primary hold their floors on it.

positive.$description: The soft ground of a Go chip, under text.positive.

warning.$description: The soft ground of a warning chip, such as a task due today, under text.warning.

negative.$description: The soft ground of a negative chip, such as an overdue task, under text.negative.

accent.$description: Shapes filled or drawn in the accent colour, such as an Ok glyph, a Go dot and the bar that marks the current item.

secondary.$description: A quiet fill: a finished or stale mark, a Done dot.

negative.$description: The destructive and failed fill: a Blocked dot.

warning.$description: Waiting, working, needs attention: a Warn dot.

amber.$description: One of the colours an application gives its areas and goals; each holds 3:1 on the sidebar.

sky.$description: One of the colours an application gives its areas and goals.

coral.$description: One of the colours an application gives its areas and goals.

sand.$description: One of the colours an application gives its areas and goals.

backdrop.$description: The veil behind a modal dialog or a sheet.

default.$description: The colour of the soft drop under what floats.

ring.$description: The hairline ring around what floats.
